title: Equilibrium, and what an increase in demand does
caption: Equilibrium is where the curves cross: P = 20, Q = 60 for the worked example. Above it there is a surplus that pushes price down. If demand increases (D → D₂), price and quantity both rise, to P = 25, Q = 70.
alt: Supply and demand diagram with price on the vertical axis and quantity on the horizontal. Demand and supply cross at price 20, quantity 60. Demand shifting right moves equilibrium to price 25, quantity 70.
description: Price is on the vertical axis and quantity on the horizontal axis, as is conventional in economics.
The demand curve D (Qd = 100 − 2P) slopes down; the supply curve S (Qs = 20 + 2P) slopes up. They cross at the equilibrium E: price 20, quantity 60.
At a price of 30, quantity supplied (80) is greater than quantity demanded (40): a surplus of 40, shown by a double-headed arrow, which pushes the price down towards equilibrium.
A dashed curve D₂ (Qd = 120 − 2P) shows an increase in demand. It crosses supply at E₂: price 25, quantity 70. Both price and quantity have risen.
